_note: Statutory auto liability minimums, one row per state per coverage, each with its official source. Arizona was read from the statute text on 2026-09-14; Nevada, Utah and Idaho were confirmed by the client on 2026-09-15. The seed adds a row only where the state has no row for that product and coverage.

rows.note: A.R.S. § 28-4009(A)(2)(b), policies issued or renewed from July 1, 2020.

arizona.notableRegulatory: At-fault state. Carriers must offer uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage at the liability limits; declining it must be in writing. Proof of financial responsibility is checked against the state database at registration.

rows.note: Nevada Division of Insurance; SB 308 (2017), effective July 1, 2018.

nevada.notableRegulatory: At-fault state. Carriers must offer uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage at least equal to the liability limits; it can be rejected in writing. Lapses are reported to the DMV, which suspends registration and charges reinstatement fees; an SR-22 filing is required after certain suspensions.

rows.note: Utah Code § 31A-22-304; a combined single limit of $80,000 also satisfies the requirement.

rows.coverage: Personal injury protection (no-fault medical), per person
rows.note: Utah is a no-fault state: PIP pays the first medical expenses regardless of fault.

utah.notableRegulatory: No-fault state: personal injury protection is mandatory and pays your own medical expenses first, and a lawsuit against the other driver is limited until a threshold is met. Uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage must be offered.

rows.note: Idaho Department of Insurance; Idaho Code § 49-1212.

idaho.notableRegulatory: At-fault state. Carriers must offer uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage, which can be rejected in writing. Insurance status is verified electronically against registrations, and an uninsured vehicle's registration can be suspended.
